title: Rethink the take-profit-at-50% rule: would you open this trade today?
summary: A common rule says close a trade at 50% of max profit. The speaker calls it one of the worst rules because it uses the past to decide. Treat the open trade as a new one and ask: would I put it on today? If it can still make 50% with an 80% probability, keeping it may be a good trade. Weigh asymmetry, probability and other opportunities.

params.label: Excess drift over rate
params.help: Your view of annual return above the risk-free rate. Zero = the market view; EV is then about zero.

steps.caption: A put credit spread already at 50% of max profit, with 21 days left.

Probability of profit from here. If it is about 80% for the rest, it may be worth keeping.
Expected value from here decides it: would you open this trade today at this price?

takeaways: Closing at 50% of max profit is a decision based on the past.
Look at the open trade as if it were new: would you put it on today?
If it can still make 50% with about 80% probability, it may be a good trade to keep.
Also weigh asymmetry and the other trades available to you.
caveats: The spread and its numbers are illustrative; the clip names no position.
The speaker says taking profits at 50% is not always wrong.
